newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to consult Egypt on Israel Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to consult Egypt on Israel Hebron deal.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat travels on Sunday to Cairo to consult with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak amid a flurry of diplomatic activity to wrap up a Hebron deal with Israel, PLO officials said.
"President Arafat is expected to visit Egypt on Sunday to brief President Mubarak on the latest developments on the Hebron negotiations," said Palestinian negotiator Hassan Asfour.
A senior Israeli official said Arafat was also due to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai before the accord was signed "within the next day or two".
Israeli and PLO officials have said they expected Netanyahu and Arafat to sign an agreement on the handover of 80 percent of the West Bank city of Hebron to Palestinian rule by year's end.
Hebron is the last of seven major West Bank cities occupied since the 1967 war that Israel agreed to return under a 1995 interim accord.
"We expect an agreement on Hebron to be signed within the next day or two," said David Bar Illan, Netanyahu's media adviser.
U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross was scheduled to return to the region on Monday to mediate any last-minute snags and attend the deal's signing.
Asked about a signing ceremony, Bar Illan told Reuters: "It will not take place with any kind of fanfare. After all, it's not a new agreement but rather the sealing of an existing one."
Under the interim deal, signed before Netanyahu took office in June, Israel was to have redeployed from most of Hebron some 10 months ago.

But Netanyahu delayed its implementation, demanding more stringent security arrangements to ensure the safety of 400 Jewish settlers who live among 100,000 Arabs in the city, a flashpoint of violence. Palestinians have rejected any changes to the accord.
Bar Illan said that "some corrections and changes have been made" to the original agreement. He did not elaborate.

In an apparent gesture of goodwill towards the Palestinians, Israel, reopened Hebron University on Saturday. The university had been closed last March after a series of Islamic suicide bombings in Israel killed 59 people.
